description: Wendy Sherman, former Deputy Secretary of State under the Biden Administration, states she was not convinced by Marco Rubio's rationale when discussing the Secretary of State testifying before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on the Venezuelan raid. She also voices her frustration with the Trump Administration's transparency efforts with Congressional leadership. Wendy speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rubio Set Aside What He Stands For: Wendy Sherman

author: Natalia Drozdiak, Courtney McBride
description: US, Danish and Greenlandic officials met Wednesday to discuss a new framework deal over Greenland, an attempt to satisfy President Donald Trump’s desire to see a greater American presence on the Arctic island that stops short of ceding it to the US.
title: US, Denmark Start Talks Over Greenland Deal to Assuage Trump

description: Bloomberg's Anarug Rana said that despite a positive earnings report from Microsoft, investors have high expectations and are concerned about the company's record spending on AI hardware. Rana says that risks remain in the tech space as companies fight it to become the future of AI, but it is likely that the high spending will pay off for Microsoft. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Microsoft Reports Record Spend on AI Hardware, as Earnings Beat Estimates

author: Alicia Diaz
description: Some Republicans are expressing second thoughts on the immigration crackdown.
title: Minnesota Deaths Shuffle the Shutdown Politics in Congress

author: Gregory Korte
description: President Donald Trump’s deployment of National Guard troops to US cities cost taxpayers at least $496 million in 2025 — with the price tag rising to a rate of $93 million a month, according to a new accounting from the Congressional Budget Office.
title: Trump’s National Guard Deployments Costing $93 Million a Month

author: Fabiola Zerpa
description: Venezuela’s interim leader is playing to three different audiences with her plans for Venezuela’s oil sector: foreign investors, the Donald Trump administration, and her own socialist supporters. None of them is happy with it.
title: Venezuela Leader Pressed From All Sides Over Oil Industry Plans

description: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell says he has “nothing for you” on whether he will leave the Fed board when his term as chair is up in May. Powell also wouldn't say more about the DOJ probe launched by the Trump administration against the Fed.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Chair Powell Won't Say What He'll Do When Term Is Up

author: Erik Wasson, Steven T. Dennis
description: Senate Democrats are demanding new constraints on President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown in exchange for their votes to avert a potentially prolonged US government shutdown starting Saturday.
title: Democrats Demand Immigration Crackdown Curbs to Avert Shutdown

description: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell says interest rates are within a range of plausible estimate of neutral. “This normalization of our policy stance should help stabilize the labor market while allowing inflation to resume its downward trend toward 2% once the effects of tariff increases have passed," he said in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Policy Should Help Stabilize Labor Market, Chair Powell Says

description: Bloomberg's Nick Wadhams says that the US is still in 'wait and see mode' on the potential for a strike against Iran as President Trump warns Iran that a failure to restart nuclear talks could end in direct action. Wadhams says that its hard to rule anything out with this administration, since attacks on both Iran and Venezuela have 'rewrote the rules of the game' when it comes to foreign policy.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Warns Iran Time Is Running Out, Keeping Strikes on the Table

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the latest news from DC. On today's show, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Bloomberg Opinion Contributor Kathryn Edwards. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: GOP Lawmakers Press Noem to Resign | Balance of Power: Early Edition 1/28/2026

author: Myles Miller
description: Two US Border Patrol agents involved in the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti have been placed on administrative leave, Customs and Border Protection said, as scrutiny intensifies over the Trump administration’s immigration-enforcement operations in Minnesota.
title: Border Patrol Agents on Leave After Fatal Minnesota Shooting

author: Todd Gillespie, Catherine Lucey
description: The US Department of Commerce is preparing to open a national artificial-intelligence center in San Francisco, putting it closer to firms at the center of some of the government’s most high-profile initiatives.
title: Commerce Department Plans National AI Center in San Francisco

description: The Federal Reserve leaves interest rates unchanged. The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 Wednesday to hold the benchmark federal funds rate in a range of 3.5%-3.75%. Governors Christopher Waller and Stephen Miran dissented. Michael McKee reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Leaves Rates Unchanged, Miran and Waller Dissent

author: Arne Delfs, Jeff Black
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he’s been closely watching the weakening dollar and is concerned about the burden it will place on Germany’s export-oriented economy.
title: Merz Seeks a More Competitive Europe to Counter the Weak Dollar

description: Kathryn Edwards, economic policy consultant and Bloomberg Opinion contributor, said the economic data doesn't give a clear reading on future rate cuts by the Fed, which also is confronting long-term issues that will affect policy. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: FOMC Tries to Parse Data From 'Inconclusive Economy,' Says Edwards

author: Brian Platt
description: Mark Carney’s Liberal Party is enjoying a surge in polls after the Canadian prime minister earned praise from other world leaders for his Davos speech urging smaller countries to resist coercion by superpowers.
title: Carney’s Liberals See Jump in Popularity After Bracing Davos Speech

author: Martha Viotti Beck, Beatriz Reis
description: Brazil will tap international debt markets more often in 2026 with bond issuances denominated in a trio of currencies, the Brazilian Treasury announced in a plan released on Wednesday.
title: Brazil to Tap Global Debt Markets in Dollars, Euros, Yuan

author: Ellen Milligan
description: The UK government is seeking to determine whether Donald Trump has the power to derail its plans to hand over sovereignty of a strategically vital island to Mauritius, after the US president called into question a deal he previously backed.
title: UK Examines Whether Trump Has Power to Derail Chagos Deal

author: Catherine Lucey, Paige Smith, Ben Steverman
description: President Donald Trump’s push to create accounts for children is getting support from financial firms including Visa Inc., which announced Wednesday that it will allow credit-card holders to use rewards points to fund those accounts.
title: Trump Lauds Visa’s Move to Use Rewards for Savings Accounts

author: Jillian Deutsch
description: Europe’s food safety regulator will publish advice on what is an acceptable level of the toxin currently at the heart of one of the biggest infant formula recalls in history.
title: Europe to Decide How Much Toxin in Baby Formula Is Too Much

author: Stephan Kueffner
description: Ecuador’s police and state prosecutors searched the homes of two recent left-wing presidential candidates in a probe over alleged laundering of illicit campaign funds from Venezuela.
title: Ecuador Probes Left-Wing Candidates Over Alleged Venezuela Cash

description: Poll data show that Trump has disappointed voters in three main areas, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Nia-Malika Henderson says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Three Charts That Show Trump’s Unpopularity

description: US Representative Ilhan Omar was charged at by a man who squirted an unknown liquid on her during a town hall in Minneapolis on Jan. 27. The man was quickly taken into custody. Omar was not hurt. The Democratic congresswoman was criticizing President Donald Trump’s aggressive immigration policies. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Rep. Omar Attacked at Town Hall in Minneapolis

description: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep rates on hold today, but the real suspense will come when we hear from Chair Jerome Powell who is clashing with the White House on a number of issues. Michael McKee reports on what to watch for.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What to Watch For in the Fed Decision

author: Anthony Hughes
description: York Space Systems Inc. is touting its ability to churn out cheap satellites for the Pentagon’s Golden Dome project as a selling point for its IPO, as investors look for exposure to the estimated $175 billion in spending on the proposed missile shield.
title: Satellite Maker York Builds IPO Pitch Around Trump’s Golden Dome

author: Daniel Flatley, Anya Andrianova, George Lei
description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent touted a strong-dollar policy on Wednesday, offering the greenback support a day after comments by President Donald Trump had sent the US currency tumbling.
title: Bessent Touts a Strong Dollar After Trump Brushed Off Its Drop

description: Carlyle Group co-founder and co-chairman says Federal Chair Jerome Powell has done a good job. He says the economy is doing pretty well and inflation is under control. He speaks on Bloomberg Surveillance.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Chair Powell Has Done a Good Job, Rubenstein Says

author: Chris Dolmetsch, Michelle Kaske
description: The legal fight over New York City’s congestion pricing plan returns to court Wednesday as a federal judge hears arguments in a lawsuit seeking to prevent the Trump administration from halting tolls motorists have been paying for a year.
title: NYC’s Fight With Trump Over Congestion Toll Returns to Court

author: Caitlin Reilly
description: Taxpayers could face long waits for IRS responses to questions on a slew of complicated new tax changes this filing season, as odds of a partial government shutdown rose sharply in the wake of federal agents’ killing of a man in Minneapolis over the weekend.
title: Shutdown Threatens to Hit IRS as Trump Touts Massive Tax Refunds

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Switzerland plans a temporary increase of its value-added tax to boost spending for the military.
title: Switzerland Plans VAT Increase for 10 Years to Revamp Military

author: Craig Stirling
description: Another US downgrade any time soon would be an unusual move so quickly after Fitch Ratings stripped the country of its top score, according to the company’s chief sovereign analyst.
title: US Faces Rating Pressure But Outlook Is Stable, Fitch Chief Says

author: Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazil’s Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva returned to power vowing to revive South American political and economic unity. A regional event this week shows he’s now fighting to maintain clout in his own backyard.
title: ‘Davos of Latin America’ Sets Up Test of Lula’s Regional Clout

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Alicia A. Caldwell
description: President Donald Trump criticized Jacob Frey after the Minneapolis mayor said that he would not change the city’s immigration policies, raising doubts about a fragile detente between federal and local leaders.
title: Trump Warns Minneapolis Mayor Over Immigration Comments

author: Laura Nahmias
description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is amping up pressure on Governor Kathy Hochul to hike taxes for the richest residents and corporations, asking the state to send billions more in aid to New York City as he faces mounting budget holes.
title: Mamdani Pushes for Tax Hikes on Wealthy New Yorkers to Fill Budget Gap

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Swiss government has decided to join the European Union’s sanctions against Haiti, it said in statement.
title: Switzerland Joins EU Sanctions Against Haiti Gang Violence

author: Julian Lee
description: A second Russia-linked oil tanker lost control as it was entering the Mediterranean Sea in under a week.
title: Russia-Linked Oil Tanker Loses Control Again in Mediterranean

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: The German government expects Europe’s biggest economy to emerge from three years of stagnation in 2026, but a heavy reliance on state spending shows fostering a broader-based recovery remains a work in progress.
title: Germany Sees Economy Reviving With Government-Spending Boost

author: Lucille Liu, Alex Wickham
description: Keir Starmer pledged in Beijing to seek a more “mature” relationship with China, as he prepared to meet President Xi Jinping on the first such trip by a British prime minister in eight years.
title: Starmer Urges ‘Mature Approach’ to China Ahead of Meeting Xi

author: Katherine Doherty, Hannah Levitt
description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Bank of America Corp. said they will match the US government’s $1,000 “Trump Account” contributions for eligible employees with children born between the beginning of last year and the end of 2028.
title: JPMorgan, Bank of America Match Workers’ $1,000 Trump Account Contributions

author: Nick Wadhams
description: President Donald Trump warned Iran that time is running out to make a deal with the US, noting that a fleet of US warships entering to the region is ready to complete their mission “with speed and violence.”
title: Trump Warns Iran That Time Is Running Out as Ships Enter Region

author: Josh Wingrove, Bill Allison
description: Rick Rieder, one of the finalists to lead the Federal Reserve, has donated to some of Donald Trump’s most prominent political rivals and Democratic leaders, a history that could present a fresh test of the president’s penchant for surrounding himself with loyalists.
title: Rick Rieder’s Donations to MAGA Rivals Tests Trump’s Fed Chair Demands

author: Christine Burke, Mirette Magdy
description: After telegraphing a more pragmatic stance on spending for months, Saudi Arabia is starting to make the tough decisions. In quick succession, the kingdom has ordered sweeping reviews at its most ambitious projects spread across Neom, Jeddah, and even Riyadh.
title: Saudi Arabia Enters New Era of Restraint on Megaproject Spend

author: Dan Strumpf
description: With nations seeking to diversify away from an increasingly unpredictable US, the Indian prime minister is keen to receive all comers.
title: All Roads Lead to Modi as World Hedges Trump

author: Slav Okov
description: Bulgaria’s central bank chief said he won’t become his country’s premier.
title: ECB’s Radev Rejects Option of Becoming Interim Bulgaria Premier

author: Charlotte Hughes-Morgan, Patrick Van Oosterom
description: Rob Jetten, whose center-left D66 party won the Dutch election in October, said he’s reached a tentative agreement with key coalition partners to form a minority government.
title: Dutch Coalition Gets Tentative Deal to Form Minority Government

author: Hallie Gu, Alfred Cang
description: China has resumed purchases of Canadian canola, an early sign of a revival in the trade after the nations reached a deal this month to mend ties.
title: China Picks Up Canadian Canola Cargoes After Reset in Trade Ties

author: Thomas Escritt
description: Hungarian authorities pressed charges against Budapest Mayor Gergely Karacsony, one of the country’s most prominent opposition figures, for flouting a police ban of the annual Pride parade last year.
title: Budapest Mayor Charged for Flouting Orban’s Pride Parade Ban

author: Andrea Palasciano
description: Kaja Kallas, who leads foreign policy for the European Union, warned that a permanent rupture in transatlantic relations and the spread of “coercive power politics” requires the bloc to quickly overhaul its approach to security and take more responsibility for its own defense.
title: EU’s Top Diplomat Says Bloc’s Defense Must Be Adapted to Survive

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. 

On today's show, US President Donald Trump’s relaxed tone about the dollar selloff is fueling speculation the greenback is at the start of a longer-term decline. He said he didn’t think the greenback had weakened excessively, sending it to a four-year low.

ASML’s earnings beat, with bookings far surpassing consensus. The company announced a buyback of up to €12 billion by the end of 2028.

Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar was attacked during a town hall in Minneapolis, where tensions over federal immigration enforcement have come to a head after agents fatally shot two US citizens.
Today's guests: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure & Hetal Mehta, Chief Economist at St. James's Place (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Embraces Weaker Dollar & ASML’s Huge Beat As AI Spurs Demand | Daybreak Europe 01/28/2026

author: Alex Wickham
description: Keir Starmer stepped up his attacks on Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party ahead of a special election that could decide the prime minister’s political future.
title: Starmer Attack on Reform’s Pick Shows His Future on the Line

author: Nguyen Dieu Tu Uyen, Nguyen Xuan Quynh
description: Vietnam and the European Union are expected to announce a comprehensive strategic partnership as European Council President Antonio Costa begins his official visit to the Southeast Asian nation on Thursday.
title: Vietnam, EU Set to Announce Comprehensive Strategic Partnership

author: William Horobin, Lizzy Burden
description: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure shrugged off gyrations in the yen after chairing a meeting of his Group of Seven counterparts.
title: France’s Lescure Says Let Markets Do Their Job as Yen Fluctuates

author: Kiuyan Wong
description: Value Partners Group Ltd. honorary chairman Cheah Cheng Hye made a rare public call for democratic reforms in Hong Kong at an event attended by mainland Chinese and local officials.
title: Hong Kong Investor Tycoon Makes Rare Call for Democratic Reforms

author: Swati Gupta, Mihir Mishra
description: An influential Maharashtra politician died in a plane crash on Wednesday, creating a leadership vacuum in one of India’s most industrialized states.
title: Senior Indian Politician in Key State Killed in Plane Crash

author: William Clowes
description: Libya’s central bank is suing Zimbabwe’s finance minister and national oil company for more than $100 million, the latest development in a spiraling debt crisis that’s bedeviled the southern African nation for a quarter of a century.
title: Libya Seeks $100 Million as Zimbabwe’s Debt Disputes Deepen

author: Alastair Gale
description: A top Pentagon official arrived in Japan for talks on countering China’s military rise as the US puts pressure on its allies in Asia to increase defense spending and reduce the burden on the American military.
title: Pentagon Official Visits Japan as US Seeks More Defense Spending

author: Derek Wallbank, Myles Miller
description: US Representative Ilhan Omar was charged at by a man who appeared to squirt an unknown liquid on her during a town hall gathering in Minneapolis, as she called for consequences for the federal officials overseeing President Donald Trump’s aggressive immigration policies.
title: Representative Ilhan Omar Attacked at Town Hall in Minneapolis

author: Josh Wingrove
description: White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller said border patrol agents might not have followed the administration’s instructions in the events that led to the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti, a rare retreat from one of President Donald Trump’s top aides and immigration hardliners.
title: Miller Shifts Blame as Pretti’s Death Splinters Trump Team Unity

description: MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — A man sprayed an unknown substance on U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar before being tackled to the ground Tuesday during a town hall she was hosting in Minneapolis, where tensions over federal immigration enforcement have come to a head after agents fatally shot an intensive care nurse and a mother of three this month.
title: Man Tackled After Spraying Unknown Substance on Ilhan Omar at Minneapolis Town Hall

author: Erica Yokoyama
description: Japan’s Finance Minister said the government will coordinate with the US when necessary as they continue to respond to currency moves.
title: Japan’s Katayama Says Will Coordinate With US on FX If Needed

description: Representative Robin Kelly (D-IL) states her articles of impeachment for DHS Secretary Kristi Noem have 163 Democratic signatures and that she'd love to see Noem resign. Rep. Kelly talks about wanting ICE to get out of Minnesota, and her frustrations with DHS' rhetoric on the killing of Alex Pretti. She speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Would Love For Kristi Noem to Resign: Rep. Robin Kelly

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Donell Harvin, former DC Chief of Homeland Security & Intelligence, suggests that hopefully there will be a reset and a withdrawal of ICE agents when discussing the Trump Administration sending Tom Homan to Minnesota. Karim Sadjadpour, Carnegie Endowment for International Peace Senior Fellow, discusses whether or not the US may strike Iran as the United States' naval carrier strike group has arrived in the Middle East. Representative Robin Kelly (D-IL) talks about the push to impeach DHS Secretary Kristi Noem. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Impeachment Threat Growing for Kristi Noem | Balance of Power: Late Edition 01/27/2026

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw the test of an upgraded large-caliber multiple rocket system designed for specific attacks as the nation seeks to raise its deterrent against nuclear war, state media reported on Wednesday.
title: North Korea’s Kim Oversaw Test of New Rocket System for Attack
